title: Lymphocyte Subsets: CD4:CD8 Ratio, Th1/Th2, Tregs and NK Cells
summary: Read a lymphocyte subset panel by its denominator, interpret the CD4:CD8 ratio as a population-dependent range, and match Th1, Th2, regulatory T cells and NK cells to their markers and cytokines.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 44 Hits 2 (CD4:CD8 2:1), 4 (Th1/Th2 cytokines), 5 (Treg CD4+/CD25+/FOXP3) and 6 (NK CD16/CD56). Checked against McBride and Striker 2017, Choi 2014, Luckheeram 2012, Cools 2007, Barzaghi and Passerini 2021, Abel 2018, Chen 2024 and Jing 2015. Hit 2’s fixed “2:1” is qualified: McBride and Striker call the normal ratio poorly defined (about 1.5–2.5, varying by age, sex and population) and note that CD8 expansion as well as CD4 loss lowers the ratio in HIV (register flag rv-cd4cd8-ratio-range). The reviewer’s CD4 ~60%/CD8 ~30% are shares of CD3+ cells; the lesson shows the corresponding share of all lymphocytes from Choi 2014. Not taught: Th1 and delayed-type hypersensitivity (Hit 4; no source read in this session), Number Vault rows other than lymphocyte percentages.

objectives: Identify T, B and NK cells by CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19, CD16 and CD56, and state whether a percentage is of lymphocytes or of T cells.
Interpret the CD4:CD8 ratio as a population-dependent range and explain how HIV lowers it.
Match Th1, Th2 and regulatory T cells to their main cytokines or defining transcription factor, and describe how NK cells kill.

scenes.title: A panel that looks “wrong”
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: a lymphocyte subset report from a healthy adult volunteer — CD3+ T cells 68% of lymphocytes, CD3+CD4+ 41% of lymphocytes, CD3+CD8+ 25% of lymphocytes, CD3−CD56+ 15% of lymphocytes, CD4:CD8 ratio 1.6. A student’s note says “CD4 should be 60% — and the ratio should be exactly 2:1.” Question token: “Abnormal, or read wrong?”

cues.text: An invented report from a healthy adult: T cells sixty-eight percent of lymphocytes, CD4 forty-one percent, CD8 twenty-five percent, and a CD3-negative, CD56-positive group at fifteen percent.
A student flags it: CD4 should be sixty percent, and the ratio should be exactly two to one. This one is one point six.
Is the panel abnormal, or is it being read wrong?

scenes.title: Who is who on the panel
scenes.altText: Schematic lymphocyte pie with marker labels. T cells: CD3+, split into CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+. B cells: CD3−CD19+. NK cells: CD3−CD56+ (and often CD16+). Number card from one healthy adult cohort (Choi 2014, 294 Korean adults, single-platform flow cytometry, means as % of lymphocytes): CD3+ 67.5%, CD3+CD4+ 40.6%, CD3+CD8+ 25.2%, CD19+ B 10.4%, CD56+ NK 15.6%, CD4:CD8 ratio 1.81. Denominator card: 40.6 ÷ 67.5 ≈ 60% — CD4 cells are about 60% of T cells but about 40% of all lymphocytes.

cues.text: Flow cytometry sorts lymphocytes by their markers. T cells carry CD3, and split into CD4 and CD8 cells. B cells are CD3-negative and CD19-positive. NK cells are CD3-negative and CD56-positive.

In one cohort of 294 healthy Korean adults, mean values were: T cells about sixty-eight percent of lymphocytes, CD4 cells about forty-one, CD8 cells about twenty-five, B cells about ten and NK cells about sixteen percent.
Now watch the denominator. Forty-one out of sixty-eight is about sixty percent. So CD4 cells are roughly sixty percent of T cells, but only about forty percent of all lymphocytes.
Values shift with age, sex and population, so each population needs its own reference values.

scenes.title: When the ratio moves
scenes.altText: Ratio card (McBride and Striker 2017): the normal CD4/CD8 ratio is poorly defined; ratios of 1.5–2.5 are generally considered normal, with wide variation by sex, age, ethnicity, genetics, exposures and infections. An inverted ratio (<1) was seen in 8% of 20–59-year-olds and 16% of 60–94-year-olds in the cited cohort; women are less likely to have an inverted ratio. HIV card: CD8 cells typically rise before CD4 cells fall, so the ratio drops early; untreated HIV drives the ratio lower; on antiretroviral therapy some patients normalise, others keep high CD8 counts and a low ratio despite viral suppression. A low or inverted ratio is an “immune risk phenotype” linked to immune senescence and chronic inflammation. MHC reminder token: CD4 + class II, CD8 + class I.

cues.text: The CD4 to CD8 ratio has no single normal value. A 2017 review calls it poorly defined: ratios of about one and a half to two and a half are generally considered normal, and sex, age, ethnicity, genetics and infections can all shift it.
An inverted ratio, below one, becomes more common with age: eight percent of adults aged twenty to fifty-nine and sixteen percent of those aged sixty to ninety-four in one cited cohort.
In HIV, CD8 cells usually rise first, before CD4 cells fall, so the ratio drops early. Untreated infection keeps driving it lower.
On treatment, some patients normalise the ratio, but others keep high CD8 counts and a low ratio even with suppressed virus. A low ratio is linked to immune ageing and chronic inflammation.

props.label: Reminder: CD4 + class II · CD8 + class I

scenes.title: Helpers, peacekeepers, natural killers
scenes.altText: Three subset cards. Th1 (master regulator T-bet): mainly IFN-γ, lymphotoxin-α and IL-2; IFN-γ activates macrophages; elimination of intracellular pathogens. Th2 (GATA3): IL-4, IL-5, IL-9, IL-13 and others; IL-4 drives IgE switching; IL-5 activates eosinophils; helminths and allergic disease. Treg: CD4+CD25+, about 5–10% of peripheral CD4 cells; CD25 also appears on activated T cells, FOXP3 is a more exclusive intracellular marker and controls Treg function; FOXP3 mutation causes IPEX, in which Treg-like cells may be present but dysfunctional. NK card: CD3−, CD56+; most blood NK cells are CD56dim and many express CD16 (FcγRIII, an IgG Fc receptor) for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; they kill without prior antigen exposure and attack cells with missing or reduced MHC class I. Hook answer token.

cues.text: Th1 cells, driven by T-bet, mainly secrete interferon gamma, lymphotoxin alpha and interleukin 2. Interferon gamma activates macrophages against intracellular pathogens.
Th2 cells, driven by GATA3, secrete interleukin 4, 5 and 13, among others. Interleukin 4 drives IgE switching, and interleukin 5 activates eosinophils, against helminths and in allergy.

Regulatory T cells are CD4 and CD25 positive, about five to ten percent of CD4 cells. CD25 also appears on activated T cells; the transcription factor FOXP3 is the more exclusive marker. FOXP3 mutation causes IPEX, where Treg-like cells can be present but suppress poorly.

NK cells are CD3-negative and CD56-positive. Many carry CD16, a receptor for the Fc part of IgG, used for antibody-dependent killing. They need no prior antigen exposure and attack cells that lack MHC class one or carry too little of it.
The hook panel is normal. It was simply read against the wrong denominator.

props.title: NK: CD3− CD56+
lines: Kills when MHC class I is missing

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “CD4 should be 60% of lymphocytes” (✓ about 60% of T cells; about 40% of lymphocytes in one healthy adult cohort — check the denominator); “CD25+ means Treg” (✓ activated T cells express CD25 too; FOXP3 is the more exclusive marker); “NK cells are CD3+ and need prior sensitisation” (✓ CD3−, CD56+, often CD16+; no prior antigen exposure needed).

cues.text: Trap one: CD4 should be sixty percent of lymphocytes. No: that figure is a share of T cells. Of all lymphocytes it is nearer forty percent in one adult cohort.
Trap two: CD25 positive means regulatory T cell. No: activated T cells carry CD25 too. FOXP3 is the more exclusive marker.
Trap three: NK cells are CD3-positive and need prior sensitisation. No: they are CD3-negative, CD56-positive, and kill without prior exposure.

props.title: ✗ “CD25+ = Treg.”
lines: ✓ Activated T cells too; FOXP3 is better

scenes.title: One inside, Two outside, Fox keeps peace
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Th ONE fights INSIDE (IFN-γ arms macrophages against intracellular pathogens); Th TWO throws OUT (IL-4 and IL-5: IgE and eosinophils against worms); the FOX keeps the PEACE (FOXP3 Tregs); NK needs NO introduction (no prior exposure).” Tokens for each. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: Th one fights inside, with interferon gamma arming macrophages. Th two throws out, with interleukin 4 and 5 bringing IgE and eosinophils. The fox, FOXP3, keeps the peace. And NK cells need no introduction.

Where it breaks: there are more helper subsets than two, such as Th17 and follicular helpers; FOXP3 can also appear in activated human T cells; and NK cells are still checked by MHC class one, so no introduction does not mean no recognition.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “CD4 ≈ 60% of T cells, ≈ 40% of lymphocytes · ratio about 1.5–2.5, varies”, “Th1 IFN-γ · Th2 IL-4/IL-5 · Treg FOXP3 · NK CD3− CD16/CD56”.

props.label: CD4 ≈ 60% of T cells, ≈ 40% of lymphocytes · ratio is a range
Th1 IFN-γ · Th2 IL-4/IL-5 · Treg FOXP3 · NK CD3− CD16/CD56

explanation.what: Plain language: lymphocytes come in families that wear different surface tags. A flow cytometer counts each family, but a percentage only makes sense once you know what it is a percentage of. Helper T cells come in types that release different signals, regulatory T cells calm the response, and NK cells kill abnormal cells without prior training. Scientific terms: CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19, CD56, CD16 (FcγRIII), CD4:CD8 ratio, inverted ratio, Th1 (T-bet; IFN-γ, IL-2), Th2 (GATA3; IL-4, IL-5, IL-13), regulatory T cell (CD4+CD25+FOXP3+), IPEX, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), missing self.
explanation.why: A CD4 percentage reported per lymphocyte looks low if compared with a figure quoted per T cell. The ratio varies widely in healthy people and falls in HIV partly because CD8 cells expand. CD25 is shared with activated T cells, so FOXP3 is used to identify Tregs, and FOXP3 loss of function breaks tolerance.
explanation.measure: One healthy adult cohort (Choi 2014, means, % of lymphocytes): CD3+ 67.5, CD4 40.6, CD8 25.2, B 10.4, NK 15.6; ratio 1.81. Ratio of about 1.5–2.5 generally considered normal; inverted below 1. Tregs about 5–10% of peripheral CD4 cells. NK cells about 5–20% of circulating lymphocytes, most CD56dim.
explanation.differs: Percent of lymphocytes vs percent of T cells; Th1 (IFN-γ, macrophages, intracellular pathogens) vs Th2 (IL-4/IL-5, IgE, eosinophils, helminths); CD25 (also on activated T cells) vs FOXP3 (more exclusive); NK (CD3−, no prior exposure) vs cytotoxic T cells (CD3+CD8+, antigen-specific).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: identify CD3−CD16+CD56+ cells as NK cells, pick Th2 cytokines for an IgE/eosinophil response, name FOXP3 as the Treg transcription factor, or interpret a CD4:CD8 ratio.

mnemonic.text: Th ONE fights INSIDE (IFN-γ arms macrophages); Th TWO throws OUT (IL-4 and IL-5: IgE and eosinophils); the FOX keeps the PEACE (FOXP3 Tregs); NK needs NO introduction (no prior exposure).
mnemonic.explanation: Links each subset to its signature product or behaviour.
mnemonic.limitation: There are more helper subsets than Th1 and Th2 (Th17, Tfh and others); FOXP3 can appear in activated human T cells; NK cells are still regulated by MHC class I, so “no introduction” means no prior exposure, not no recognition.

takeaway: Check the denominator before calling a lymphocyte panel abnormal, treat the CD4 to CD8 ratio as a range rather than a fixed two to one, and match Th1 to interferon gamma, Th2 to interleukin 4 and 5, regulatory T cells to FOXP3, and natural killer cells to CD3-negative CD16 and CD56 markers.

questions.stem: A healthy adult’s flow panel reports CD3+ 70%, CD3+CD4+ 42% and CD3+CD8+ 26% of lymphocytes, CD4:CD8 ratio 1.6. Which interpretation is best?

options.text: Consistent with typical adult values; CD4 cells are about 60% of the T cells
options.rationale: Correct. 42 of 70 is 60% of T cells; the percentages and a ratio of 1.6 fall near published healthy adult means and the 1.5–2.5 range usually considered normal.

options.text: CD4 lymphopenia, because CD4 should be 60% of lymphocytes
options.rationale: Incorrect. About 60% is a share of T cells, not of all lymphocytes.
Incorrect. An inverted ratio is below 1; 1.6 is not inverted.

options.text: Abnormal, because any ratio other than exactly 2.0 is abnormal
options.rationale: Incorrect. The normal ratio is a range that varies with age, sex and population.

questions.stem: A patient with a helminth infection has eosinophilia and a raised total IgE. Which CD4 subset and cytokines best explain this pattern?

options.rationale: Correct. IL-4 drives IgE switching and IL-5 activates eosinophils; Th2 responses target helminths.
Incorrect. Th1 cytokines activate macrophages against intracellular pathogens.
Incorrect. These are suppressive cytokines; IL-10 and TGF-β suppress IgE production.
Incorrect. NK cells are not CD4 helper cells; perforin and granzymes mediate killing.

questions.stem: Which statement about identifying regulatory T cells is correct?

options.text: FOXP3 is a more exclusive intracellular marker than CD25, which activated T cells also express
options.rationale: Correct. CD25 and other activation markers are not exclusive to Tregs; FOXP3 is the more exclusive marker and controls Treg function.
Incorrect. Activated T cells can express CD25 too.

options.text: Tregs make up most of the peripheral CD4 cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. Naturally occurring CD4+CD25+ Tregs are about 5–10% of peripheral CD4 cells.

options.text: In IPEX, CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ cells are always absent from blood
options.rationale: Incorrect. Depending on the mutation, Treg-like cells can be present at normal frequency but fail to suppress, so function and FOXP3 studies matter.
